local_stories.title: Cindy makes 1,000 dumplings a day. This is how she gets the perfect pleat – video
local_stories.simplified_title: Melbourne chef shows how to make perfect dumplings for Lunar New Year
local_stories.simplified_body:
Cindy Feng, a chef in Melbourne, makes 1,000 dumplings every day and is sharing her technique as Chinese communities celebrate Lunar New Year.

Dumplings are a symbolic food during this festival, and Feng shows that making them perfectly requires both skill and patience, not just speed. She demonstrates the precise way to fold and pleat each dumpling.

The video is part of celebrations happening across Australia as communities mark one of the most important festivals in the Chinese calendar.
local_stories.quick_summary: A Melbourne dumpling chef demonstrates the careful technique behind making traditional dumplings for Lunar New Year celebrations.
local_stories.description:
As Lunar New Year celebrations get under way, attention in some Chinese communities turns to one of the festival’s most symbolic foods – the dumpling. Melbourne dumpling chef Cindy Feng demonstrates how to shape them with care and precision, and explains why technique, as much as speed, matters

local_stories.title: Man fined $30,000 for poaching rare Queensland rainforest python
local_stories.simplified_title: Man fined $30,000 for stealing rare pythons from Queensland rainforest
local_stories.simplified_body:
A man has been fined $30,000 for stealing eight rare pythons from a rainforest in Cape York, in far north Queensland.

Clinton Spiteri went to the rainforest with two other people to take the snakes, which are protected because they are rare and only found in certain Queensland rainforests. Taking wildlife from protected areas is illegal because it threatens species that are already struggling to survive.

The court heard evidence about the poaching trip. The large fine is meant to deter others from stealing protected wildlife.
local_stories.quick_summary: Clinton Spiteri was fined for poaching eight rare snakes from a Cape York rainforest with two other people.
local_stories.description: The court heard Clinton Spiteri was with two others when he visited a rainforest in the Cape York area to steal eight snakes. | Also reported by: ABC News Australia

local_stories.title: Ex-cop granted bail over alleged stalking following neighbour dispute
local_stories.simplified_title: Former Queensland police officer gets bail after allegedly harassing neighbours
local_stories.simplified_body:
A former Queensland police officer has been granted bail after being charged with allegedly stalking and harassing his neighbours.

The court heard he allegedly wore a balaclava (a mask that covers the face) and an Easter bonnet (a decorative hat) while intimidating a family living nearby. The charges stem from a dispute between neighbours that apparently escalated.

Being granted bail means he can stay out of jail while waiting for his trial, but he will likely have conditions he must follow, such as staying away from the neighbours.
local_stories.quick_summary: A former Queensland police officer accused of wearing disguises to intimidate a neighbouring family has been released on bail.
local_stories.description: A former Queensland police officer accused of allegedly wearing a balaclava and Easter bonnet to harass and intimidate a neighbouring family has been granted bail.

local_stories.simplified_title: Queensland's proposed hate speech laws face criticism over free speech concerns
local_stories.simplified_body:
The Institute of Public Affairs, a rightwing thinktank (a research organisation that develops policy ideas), has raised concerns about Queensland's proposed hate speech laws.

The organisation says the laws are too vague and could restrict free speech. Critics from across the political spectrum — both left and right — are worried the laws don't clearly define what counts as hate speech, which could lead to unfair penalties or people being afraid to speak freely.

The Queensland government will need to address these concerns if it wants the laws to pass. The debate highlights the difficult balance between protecting people from harmful speech and preserving freedom of expression.
local_stories.quick_summary: A rightwing thinktank has joined others in criticising Queensland's proposed hate speech laws as too vague and threatening to free speech.

local_stories.title: Rightwing thinktank joins backlash to Queensland’s ‘vague’ proposed hate speech laws
local_stories.simplified_title: Child vaccination rates drop below target in Australia, raising disease risk
local_stories.simplified_body:
Childhood vaccination rates in Australia are falling fast, with some regions barely reaching 80% coverage.

Before COVID-19, Australia achieved its target of 95% of one-year-olds being fully immunised against diseases like whooping cough and measles. Lower vaccination rates mean more babies are now at risk of catching these serious, sometimes deadly, diseases. When fewer children are vaccinated, diseases can spread more easily through communities.

Health experts are concerned about why rates have dropped and are working to encourage parents to vaccinate their children on schedule to protect both individual kids and the wider community.
local_stories.quick_summary: Australia's childhood vaccination rates have fallen from 95% to around 80% in some areas, putting more babies at risk of serious diseases.
local_stories.description:

national_stories.simplified_title: Long COVID continues to affect Australians as federal funding is reduced
national_stories.simplified_body:
Long COVID — ongoing symptoms after a COVID-19 infection — is still affecting many Australians, even as public attention has moved on.

One person describes how their life came to a stop because of long COVID, which can cause more than 200 different symptoms and is difficult to diagnose and treat. The federal government has reduced funding for long COVID research and support, leaving patients feeling abandoned and questioning whether their illness is being taken seriously.

Without proper funding and research, people with long COVID may struggle to get the medical care and support they need to recover or manage their symptoms.
national_stories.quick_summary: A person with long COVID describes how the condition stopped their life, while reduced government funding leaves patients asking if their illness is being taken seriously.
national_stories.description: Before COVID, Australia reached its target of 95% of one-year-olds fully immunised. Now, lower coverage means more babies are at risk of whooping cough and measles.

national_stories.title: Long Covid is still here. I know – my life came to a stop because of it
national_stories.simplified_title: Real wages fall as $100,000 salary loses value due to inflation
national_stories.simplified_body:
By 2025, 45% of full-time workers in Australia earned $100,000 or more per year, but years of high inflation mean this milestone doesn't mean what it once did.

Real wages — what your salary can actually buy after accounting for rising prices — have gone backwards. Even though more people are earning six figures, the cost of housing, food, and other essentials has risen so much that these salaries don't stretch as far as they did a few years ago.

This means many workers feel financially squeezed despite earning what used to be considered a very good income.
national_stories.quick_summary: Even though more Australians earn six-figure salaries, high inflation means $100,000 doesn't buy as much as it used to.
national_stories.description:
With more than 200 possible symptoms, long Covid isn’t easy to treat and diagnose. Rolled-back federal funding has led longhaulers to ask: is this all in my head?

I am 30ft below the surface of the Blue Grotto, a crystalline diving hole in central Florida. Between the water’s embrace and the restriction of my wetsuit, my blood pressure finally stabilizes. The long, deep breaths I pull from my respirator keep my heart rate nice and low.

I feel lighter than I have since April 2022, when I first contracted long Covid. I feel childlike at the fact that I can do this at all – get scuba certified – when on land I’m often confined to a wheelchair or a walker.

national_stories.simplified_title: New report finds widespread racism at Australian universities
national_stories.simplified_body:
A new report has found that racism is widespread at Australian universities, with institutions failing to meet their duty of care to protect students and staff.

Duty of care means universities have a legal and moral responsibility to keep people safe and treat them fairly. The report found that many universities are not doing enough to prevent or address racist incidents, leaving students and staff from diverse backgrounds feeling unsafe and unsupported.

Experts say universities need to take stronger action, including better policies, training, and support systems, to tackle racism on campuses.
national_stories.quick_summary: A new report reveals that racism is common at Australian universities and that institutions have failed in their duty of care to students and staff.
national_stories.description: By 2025, 45% of full-time workers in Australia had ‘six figure’ earnings. But years of high inflation mean cracking this threshold doesn’t mean what it used to.

national_stories.title: ‘Not met their duty of care’: new report finds racism is widespread at Australian unis
national_stories.simplified_title: Coalition leads in Victoria as One Nation surges to 21% support
national_stories.simplified_body:
The Coalition (the Liberal and National parties working together) is leading in Victoria with 29% support, according to a new DemosAU poll.

Surprisingly, One Nation — a minor party known for its hardline immigration and nationalist policies — is polling at 21%, just two points behind the Labor Party. This is a significant jump for One Nation and suggests some voters are turning away from the major parties.

The Victorian state election is nine months away in November, so these numbers could still change, but they show a tight race and growing support for minor parties.
national_stories.quick_summary: A new poll shows the Coalition ahead in Victoria at 29%, while One Nation has jumped to 21%, just two points behind Labor.

national_stories.title: The Coalition leads in Victorian DemosAU poll, with One Nation posting 21% support
national_stories.simplified_title: Disappearances in Mexico surge 200% as drug cartels expand
national_stories.simplified_body:
Disappearances in Mexico have surged by 200% over the past 10 years, with more than 130,000 people now considered missing or disappeared.

Many disappearances are linked to drug cartels — powerful criminal organisations that control drug trafficking and often use violence and kidnapping. The story describes how Ángel Montenegro, a 31-year-old construction worker, was dragged into a van by several men in 2022 and hasn't been seen since.

The crisis is worsening as cartels expand their territory and power, leaving families desperate for answers and the government struggling to address the violence.
national_stories.quick_summary: More than 130,000 people are now missing or disappeared in Mexico, a 200% increase over 10 years as drug cartels grow more powerful.
national_stories.description: The Coalition is pulling ahead in Victoria, polling at 29%, while One Nation is just two points behind Labor, nine months out from the November election.

global_stories.simplified_title: Global corruption watchdog reports increase in graft worldwide
global_stories.simplified_body:
A global corruption watchdog called Transparency International has reported an increase in corruption (dishonest behaviour by people in power, often involving bribery) around the world.

Countries that were once seen as having low corruption — including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Sweden — are now slipping backwards. The organisation says this is happening because of a lack of strong political leadership willing to fight corruption.

The Corruption Perception Index measures how corrupt countries are seen to be. Rising corruption can undermine trust in government and make it harder for countries to function fairly.
global_stories.quick_summary: Transparency International's annual report shows corruption is rising globally, with countries like the US, UK, Canada, and Sweden slipping due to weak political leadership.
global_stories.description:
More than 130,000 people considered missing or disappeared in Mexico as drug cartels expand

It was a bright morning in August 2022 when Ángel Montenegro was taken. A 31-year-old construction worker, Montenegro had been out all night drinking with some work buddies in the city of Cuautla and was waiting for a bus back to nearby Cuernavaca, where he lived.

At about 10am, a white van pulled up: several men jumped out and dragged Montenegro and a co-worker inside before speeding off. Montenegro’s co-worker was released a few hundred meters down the street, but Montenegro was driven away.

global_stories.simplified_title: Israel speeds up West Bank annexation as Trump's influence remains unclear
global_stories.simplified_body:
Israel is accelerating its annexation of the West Bank — taking control of Palestinian land and forcing people out at a faster rate than ever before.

The West Bank is Palestinian territory that Israel has occupied since 1967. Annexation means officially claiming the land as part of Israel, which is illegal under international law. Palestinians are being pushed off their lands, losing homes and livelihoods.

It's unclear whether US President Donald Trump will try to stop this. Past US presidents have sometimes pressured Israel on this issue, but Trump's position remains uncertain.
global_stories.quick_summary: Israel is forcing Palestinians out of the West Bank at an unprecedented rate, raising questions about whether Donald Trump will intervene.
global_stories.description: Once seen as anti-graft strongholds, the US, UK, Canada and Sweden are slipping into decline due to a lack of political leadership, Transparency International's Corruption Perception Index has revealed.

global_stories.title: Israel is accelerating its creeping annexation of the West Bank. Can Donald Trump stop it?
global_stories.simplified_title: Chicago mourns civil rights leader Jesse Jackson after his death
global_stories.simplified_body:
People in Chicago are mourning the death of Jesse Jackson, a major civil rights leader who spent decades fighting for equality and justice.

Jackson was a key figure in the American civil rights movement, which fought to end racial discrimination and secure equal rights for Black Americans. He was particularly influential in Chicago, where his activism shaped the community and inspired generations of people to fight for social justice.

Residents told the BBC they will always be grateful for his work and legacy. His death marks the end of an era for the civil rights movement.
global_stories.quick_summary: Residents of Chicago are mourning the death of civil rights leader Jesse Jackson, reflecting on how his activism shaped their community.
global_stories.description: Israel’s actions are forcing Palestinians out of their lands at an unprecedented rate.

global_stories.title: 'We're going to always be grateful' - Chicagoans mourn loss of Jesse Jackson
global_stories.simplified_title: Ukraine peace talks stall as Zelenskyy accuses Russia of delaying negotiations
global_stories.simplified_body:
Peace talks between Ukraine and Russia ended abruptly after about two hours today, with no progress on major issues.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of deliberately dragging out the negotiations. The unresolved issues include what happens to territories in eastern Ukraine that Russia currently occupies and control of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, Europe's largest nuclear facility.

The talks are much shorter than yesterday's six-hour session, suggesting tensions remain high. Without agreement on these sensitive issues, the war that has devastated Ukraine since Russia's invasion is likely to continue.
global_stories.quick_summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says peace talks with Russia ended abruptly with no agreement on key issues, accusing Russia of dragging out negotiations.

The peace talks ended abruptly today after about two hours, according to reports, in contrast with yesterday’s negotiations that apparently took place over six hours.

Neither side have offered any public sign of progress, but instead said the talks were “difficult” with Russian news agencies quoting sources describing the negotiations as “very tense”.
